# std.fetch

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Outbound HTTP(S) requests, run on the blocking pool (the calling task
parks). Every status is a reply, not an error. `get`/`post`/... and
`Client` read text bodies and follow no redirects; `send` takes any
`Request` (method, headers, a byte body, redirects to follow, a body
limit) and gives a `Response` with a byte body and JSON helpers.

## Types

### `Client`

```badger
struct Client { origin: String, timeout_ms: Int }
```

Authority to make requests to one origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), and
no other: request paths must start with a single `/`. A capability the
entry module of a restricted project can hand out.

#### `Client.delete`

```badger
fn delete(self: &Self, path: String) -> Result<Reply, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

#### `Client.get`

```badger
fn get(self: &Self, path: String) -> Result<Reply, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

#### `Client.origin`

```badger
fn origin(self: &Self) -> String
```

The origin it may reach.

#### `Client.post`

```badger
fn post(self: &Self, path: String, body: String, content_type: String) -> Result<Reply, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

#### `Client.put`

```badger
fn put(self: &Self, path: String, body: String, content_type: String) -> Result<Reply, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

#### `Client.send`

```badger
fn send(self: &Self, path: String, r: Request) -> Result<Response, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

Send `r` to `path` on this client's origin (its own `url` is
replaced); redirects are never followed, as they could leave the
origin.

#### `Client.timeout`

```badger
fn timeout(self: &Self, limit: Duration) -> Client
```

The same client with another time limit per request.

### `Reply`

```badger
pub type Reply = { status: Int, headers: List<(String, String)>, body: String }
```

### `Request`

```badger
pub type Request = {
```

A request: any method, headers, a byte body, a time limit, how many
redirects to follow (none by default), and the largest reply body to
read (16 MiB by default; more is `:io/too_large`).

### `Response`

```badger
struct Response { pub status: Int, pub headers: List<(String, String)>, pub body: Bytes, pub url: String }
```

A reply: every status is one (not an error); the body is bytes, and
`url` is where it came from after any redirects.

#### `Response.header`

```badger
fn header(self: &Self, name: String) -> Option<String>
```

The first value of a header (names compare case-insensitively).

#### `Response.is_success`

```badger
fn is_success(self: &Self) -> Bool
```

Whether the status is 2xx.

#### `Response.json`

```badger
fn json<T>(self: &Self) -> Result<T, io.Error> where T: Codec
```

The body decoded from JSON as `T`.

#### `Response.text`

```badger
fn text(self: &Self) -> Result<String, io.Error>
```

The body as UTF-8 text.

## Functions

### `client`

```badger
fn client(base: String) -> Result<Client, io.Error> !{Io}
```

A client for `base`, an `http` or `https` origin.

### `get`

```badger
fn get(url: String) -> Result<Reply, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

`GET url` (30 s limit).

### `get_json`

```badger
fn get_json<T>(url: String) -> Result<T, io.Error> !{Io, Wait} where T: Codec
```

`GET url` and decode a 2xx reply's JSON body as `T` (another status
is an `:io/http_status` error).

### `post`

```badger
fn post(url: String, body: String, content_type: String) -> Result<Reply, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

`POST url` with a body of `content_type` (30 s limit).

### `post_json`

```badger
fn post_json<T, R>(url: String, value: T) -> Result<R, io.Error> !{Io, Wait} where T: Codec, R: Codec
```

`POST url` with `value` as JSON, decoding a 2xx reply's JSON as `R`.

### `request`

```badger
fn request(method: String, url: String) -> Request
```

A request of `method` to `url` with the defaults (no body, 30 s, no
redirects followed, 16 MiB).

### `send`

```badger
fn send(r: Request) -> Result<Response, io.Error> !{Io, Wait}
```

Send `r`.
